```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->

Nanopore reads from the black band disease (BBD) metagenome were assembled using `Flye` in metagenome mode. Commands for this stage were run from the `flye/` directory.

A symbolic link to the BBD nanopore read file was added to ensure that the sequencing is accessed without duplicating the large input file: 
```{bash}
ln -s /pvol/data/metagenome_assembly/bbd_0.1.fastq.gz .
```

Then, the `flye` assembly was run using the slurm shell script `run_flye_bbd.sh`, and the slurm job output was assessed:
```{bash}
sbatch run_flye_bbd.sh

ls -l bbd/assembly.fasta
```

The completed assembly (written by `Flye`) was saved to as `assembly.fasta`.
